name: Berkshire County, MA
findings: Berkshire County has 614 nonprofit organizations. 223 of them (36%) list at least one way to get involved in their tax returns or on their websites: membership, volunteering, public events, or civic and political action.
The most common is membership, listed by 180 organizations.
Arts and cultural organizations are the largest group offering opportunities (15% of those with an identified type).
Compared with 10 similar places, Berkshire County has about as many organizations offering opportunities per resident.

observations.title: Arts and cultural organizations stand out for membership
observations.text: 27 arts and cultural organizations here list membership, compared with about 8 in similar places of this size.

confidence.text: Based on 27 organizations here; 24% of all organizations here have no identified type.

observations.question: What role do arts and cultural organizations play in community life here? Who do they reach, and who might they miss?

observations.title: More organizations list civic or political action
observations.text: Per resident, more organizations in Berkshire County list civic or political action in their tax returns or on their websites than in 10 similar places (about 1.5 times the typical level).

confidence.text: Based on 13 organizations here; 24% of all organizations here have no identified type.

observations.question: Why are ways to take civic or political action so common here? Who takes part, and who might not be reached?

observations.title: Foundation organizations that list no opportunities
observations.text: 42 foundation organizations here list none of the four kinds of opportunity in their tax returns or on their websites. Many may still offer them without describing them there.
